question: The company matches 6% of my 401(k). Should I also open a Roth IRA, and which comes first?

figures.label: Most the match is worth, as % of pay (50% of the first 6%)
Step 1: 401(k) at 6% to get the full match
Roth IRA at the 2026 limit ($7,500), per check
Step 3: Roth IRA from this goal
Step 4: extra 401(k) with what is left
Step 2 if on the HDHP: your own HSA money to the limit, per check
figures.note: Only if the user switches to the HDHP. On the default PPO 750 the HSA step is skipped.

must_include: Corrects the premise: the company matches 50 cents per dollar on the first 6% of pay, so the match is worth 3% of pay, not 6%; you still contribute 6% to get all of it.
Step 1 is the 401(k) at 6% (about $207.69 per check) to get the full match (about $103.85 per check, $2,700 a year).
Step 2 is the HSA, but only on the HDHP; on the PPO 750 there is no HSA, so this step is skipped.
Step 3 is a Roth IRA, about $288.46 per check to reach the $7,500 2026 limit, and $90k is under the Roth income limit.
Step 4 is extra 401(k): the $600 goal leaves about $103.85 per check after steps 1 and 3.
Says the match vests 20% per year, fully after 5 years, so leaving early forfeits part of the match.
Notes the Roth IRA is opened outside work (not a payroll deduction) and the dollars per check are what to set aside each payday.
must_not_include: Putting money in a Roth IRA before getting the full 401(k) match.
Saying the match is 6% of pay.

assumptions: Savings goal of $600 per check (profile 'default'); the quiz does not ask this yet.
Profile has a 3-month emergency fund, so the order starts with retirement. With no emergency fund, see ex5-loans-vs-invest and eval/edge_cases.md.
Order (match, HSA, Roth IRA, extra 401(k)) is the common rule of thumb the proposal names; a new hire confirms it before status becomes user_confirmed.

sources.what: IRA limit $7,500; Roth IRA single phase-out $153,000-$168,000; 401(k) deferral limit $24,500
